name: ai.craterview/mcp
title: CraterView.ai
description: Enlarge, denoise and restore photos, or check if one was made by AI, on your CraterView.ai account.

tools.name: upload_photo
tools.description:
Makes an image available for viewing and jobs. Returns the image's `input_key`. Runs nothing and charges nothing.

Give one of:
- image_url, for an image already online.
- content_type and content_length, for a file on this computer that your shell can read. The answer has a `curl` command that sends it straight to storage, and the file is there once that has succeeded.
- job_id, for the result file from another job.
- image_base64, only for a very small file you cannot send any other way.

If you cannot send the image, because you can only see it in this conversation or your shell cannot reach storage, ask the user to choose the photo at https://craterview.ai/app and give you its File ID, which is the `input_key`, or for a link to it.

The `input_key` is valid for a day after the image was uploaded.

Privacy: images and results are private to the account, never used to train, tune or evaluate a model, public only if the user submits them to the gallery.

image_url.description: A public or signed http(s) link to a PNG, JPEG, WebP, HEIC, HEIF or TIFF image. Limit is 300MB.

content_type.description: For a file on this computer, with content_length: the file's type.

content_length.description: For a file on this computer, with content_type: its exact size in bytes, read in your shell so the image never enters your context. Limit is 300MB.

job_id.description: The job `id` of the result to make available for viewing and further jobs.

image_base64.description: A base64-encoded image file. Limit is 8MB decoded. This is in your context and potentially costs several million tokens. Only for a small file you cannot send any other way. An image you can only see in this conversation cannot be sent: encode the file's bytes, never what you see.

tools.name: enhance_photo
tools.description:
Enhance (cv-enhance-v3, 1 credit an image up to 6 MP, 2 credits above): Makes a photograph sharper and rebuilds fine detail enlarged up to 4 times. It is the model to suggest first for almost any photograph someone wants improved, a grainy one included. Suggest trying Denoise as well. If the photograph is noisy and being enlarged, set binning for simple noise reduction: pixel binning averages each square of 2x2, 3x3 or 4x4 pixels into one before enlarging, which takes noise out and leaves less room to enlarge. Strongly recommended: run it on the original photograph, before Denoise or Restore, because it might not work well on another model's result. Among the photographs it is right for: a soft scan, a small or cropped photograph, and anything the compression flattened. A price in MP counts the part of the image worked on, the whole image or the region sent, divided by 4 at binning 2x2, 9 at 3x3 and 16 at 4x4. The tools make an informed estimate of fine detail, so small text can come back with made-up letters and a small face as a likeness rather than the person. Tell the user before they rely on either.

Only the user starts a run: call this only after they have said to, free jobs too. "Make this sharper" asks for a result, not a run: say what you would use and what it will cost, then wait. `quote` runs nothing and is free: call it without asking.

Send the image as `input_key`: upload_photo answers with one.

An answer's `job` is the job as the API states it. On a finished job, `usage` is the account as get_usage answers it.

Most images finish inside this call, with links in `job.result.output` and a small preview of the result to check it by. A slower one answers with `job.status` queued or running: collect it with get_job and `job.id`. Calling this tool again would run the work and charge for it twice.

input_key.description: The image: the `input_key` upload_photo answered with, or a File ID the user copied from their CraterView.ai workspace.

scale.description: Enlargement factor, from 1 to 4; it need not be a whole number. The result is your image, or the region you name, this many times larger in each direction, rounded down to whole pixels. Send scale, width or height, only one; with none, the factor is 4. With binning, the largest factor is 4 divided by the block's side, and that is the default: 2 at 2x2, 4/3 at 3x3 and 1 at 4x4. The image and the result must fit your key's limits; if not, name a smaller region or enlarge less.

width.description: The width of the result in pixels, instead of a scale; the height keeps the proportions of your image or region. From 1 to 4 times the width worked on, or with binning from 1 to 4 divided by the block's side. Send width, height or scale, only one.

height.description: The height of the result in pixels, instead of a scale; the width keeps the proportions of your image or region. From 1 to 4 times the height worked on, or with binning from 1 to 4 divided by the block's side. Send width, height or scale, only one.

roi.description: The part of the image to work on, as fractions of the width and height of **the image you send**, from the top left. Everything outside it is discarded first, so a region is how a large image fits your key's limits at full detail. Omit it for the whole image. If you cropped the file yourself, use the cropped image's coordinates, not the original's. A region past an edge is trimmed to the image.

binning.description: Simple noise reduction by pixel binning of your image or region before it is enlarged: off, or 2x2, 3x3 or 4x4, where each square block of that many pixels is averaged into one. Binning takes noise out, more with a larger block, and costs enlargement: the largest scale is 4 divided by the block's side, 2 at 2x2, 4/3 at 3x3 and 1 at 4x4, and that is the scale you get if you send no size. In return the image or region may be larger by the block's area. It is for a noisy photograph you are enlarging, from low light or a high ISO, and never a way to fit a larger clean image: on a clean one it redraws the finest texture, so name a region with roi instead. To take noise out without enlarging, use Denoise, which does that much better.

output_format.description: The format of the result. auto keeps the format you sent, except HEIC and HEIF, which prefer JPEG, and TIFF, which comes back as PNG. Any format is a preference, and the result is PNG where it cannot hold the image whole: JPEG holds no alpha channel and at most 65,500 pixels a side, WebP at most 16,383 pixels a side, and both 8 bits per channel. A deeper image keeps its depth, colours keep their space, and greyscale comes back as colour (RGB). WebP halves colour resolution; PNG and JPEG keep it whole. result.output.content_type says which format came back.

quality.description: Encoder quality for jpeg and webp.

params.description:
Settings for this model. Leave out anything not asked for: each has a default.

scale: left out, the largest factor whose result fits inside the model's size limit for this account is used — not the model's own default, which a whole photograph usually cannot have.

roi: **look at the image and name the subject.** Everything outside it is discarded, so what comes back is made from this part alone — a face in a group photograph, a sign in the distance, the animal rather than the field — and it may be any shape that fits the subject. A region is how a large photograph gets the full factor on the part worth enlarging.

tools.name: redraw_small_faces
tools.description:
Small face enhancement (cv-faces-v1, 1 credit an image up to 6 faces redrawn, 2 credits above): Makes small, blurry or distorted faces look natural. For the people in a group photograph whose faces came out small and distorted after enlarging: run it on the enlarged result rather than the original. An image with no face small enough is refused and costs nothing. The tools make an informed estimate of fine detail, so small text can come back with made-up letters and a small face as a likeness rather than the person. Tell the user before they rely on either.

Only the user starts a run: call this only after they have said to, free jobs too. "Make this sharper" asks for a result, not a run: say what you would use and what it will cost, then wait. `quote` runs nothing and is free: call it without asking.

Send the image as `input_key`: upload_photo answers with one.

An answer's `job` is the job as the API states it. On a finished job, `usage` is the account as get_usage answers it.

Most images finish inside this call, with links in `job.result.output` and a small preview of the result to check it by. A slower one answers with `job.status` queued or running: collect it with get_job and `job.id`. Calling this tool again would run the work and charge for it twice.

input_key.description: The image: the `input_key` upload_photo answered with, or a File ID the user copied from their CraterView.ai workspace.

seed.description: The same seed and input reproduce the same result. Faces up to about 48 pixels tall are redrawn, twelve at most, and larger ones are left as they are. A face that small is drawn to fit the photograph, not recovered, so vary the seed for a differently drawn face.

output_format.description: The format of the result. auto keeps the format you sent, except HEIC and HEIF, which prefer JPEG, and TIFF, which comes back as PNG. A deeper image keeps its depth, colours keep their space, and greyscale comes back as colour (RGB). tools.name: make_headshot
tools.description:
Headshot (cv-headshot-v1, 1 credit an image): Turns a photograph with a face in it into a professional headshot. The tools make an informed estimate of fine detail, so small text can come back with made-up letters and a small face as a likeness rather than the person. Tell the user before they rely on either.

Only the user starts a run: call this only after they have said to, free jobs too. "Make this sharper" asks for a result, not a run: say what you would use and what it will cost, then wait. `quote` runs nothing and is free: call it without asking.

roi.description: The part of the photograph the person is in, as fractions of the width and height of **the image you send**, from the top left. Everything outside it is discarded first, and the headshot is made from the largest face inside it, so a region chooses the person in a photograph of several. Omit it for the whole photograph. If you cropped the file yourself, use the cropped image's coordinates, not the original's. A region past an edge is trimmed to the image.

attire.description: business: a dark jacket over a plain shirt. as-is: the clothes they are wearing. Both use the headshot's backdrop, lighting and framing, and remove sunglasses, hats and anything in front of the face. starship-captain: a dark high-collared uniform on a starship's bridge, with pointed ears and upswept eyebrows. Their hairstyle, facial hair, age, face shape and expression are kept.

seed.description: The same seed and input reproduce the same result. Vary it to get a different headshot from the same photograph.

Any format is a preference, and the result is PNG where it cannot hold the image whole: JPEG holds no alpha channel and at most 65,500 pixels a side, WebP at most 16,383 pixels a side, and both 8 bits per channel. A deeper image keeps its depth, colours keep their space, and greyscale comes back as colour (RGB). The result has no transparency. WebP halves colour resolution; PNG and JPEG keep it whole. result.output.content_type says which format came back.

To make a noisy photograph larger, use Enhance with binning on the original instead: it might not work well on this model's result. tools.name: restore_photo
tools.description:
Restore (cv-restore-v1, 1 credit an image): Tears, creases, scratches, dust and grain are removed and washed-out colour is corrected. The photograph comes back at its own size, or enlarged up to 4 times with scale. Prefer enhance_photo for enlargements and try denoise_photo for very noisy images. Before a black-and-white photograph of people is returned in colour, ask the user who is in it and what they know of its colours, and send that as `context`. Without `context`, every colour, skin tone and damaged detail is a guess. The tools make an informed estimate of fine detail, so small text can come back with made-up letters and a small face as a likeness rather than the person. Tell the user before they rely on either.

Only the user starts a run: call this only after they have said to, free jobs too. "Make this sharper" asks for a result, not a run: say what you would use and what it will cost, then wait. `quote` runs nothing and is free: call it without asking.

Send the image as `input_key`: upload_photo answers with one.

An answer's `job` is the job as the API states it. On a finished job, `usage` is the account as get_usage answers it.

Most images finish inside this call, with links in `job.result.output` and a small preview of the result to check it by. A slower one answers with `job.status` queued or running: collect it with get_job and `job.id`. Calling this tool again would run the work and charge for it twice.

input_key.description: The image: the `input_key` upload_photo answered with, or a File ID the user copied from their CraterView.ai workspace.

roi.description: The part of the photograph to repair, as fractions of the width and height of **the image you send**, from the top left. Everything outside it is discarded first, and the part comes back at its own size, or enlarged by scale; a region is how a large photograph fits your key's limits when enlarged. In a very small part, well under a megapixel, small details can come back changed. Omit it for the whole photograph. If you cropped the file yourself, use the cropped image's coordinates, not the original's. A region past an edge is trimmed to the image.

monochrome.description: Set for a black-and-white photograph: it is returned black and white and the repair is more conservative. Left unset, a black-and-white photograph is returned in colour.

context.description: What you know that the image cannot show, in a sentence: who the people are, the colour of what they are wearing, where and when it was taken. The repair follows it, most of all when a black-and-white photograph comes back in colour: "The first Black Canadian Olympian", "A soldier in a red tunic". Up to 260 characters.

scale.description: Enlargement factor, from 1 to 4; it need not be a whole number. The result is your image, or the region you name, this many times larger in each direction, rounded down to whole pixels. At 1, the default, it comes back at its own size. An enlarged result's fine detail is drawn by the repair, not recovered from your image. The result must fit your key's limits; if not, name a smaller region or enlarge less.

seed.description: The same seed and input reproduce the same result. Vary it to get a different repair of the same photograph.

output_format.description: The format of the result. auto keeps the format you sent, except HEIC and HEIF, which prefer JPEG, and TIFF, which comes back as PNG. tools.name: check_content
tools.description:
Content Check (cv-content-check-v1, free): Screens an image against the service's content policy without changing it. `job.result.verdict` (`passed`, `flagged`): `flagged` when the image may fall outside what the service allows, `passed` when it was checked and nothing was found. The same answer as the job's `flagged` field.

This check changes nothing and costs nothing, so it needs no go-ahead: call it when its answer would help, and say what it found.

Send the image as `input_key`: upload_photo answers with one.

An answer's `job` is the job as the API states it. On a finished job, `usage` is the account as get_usage answers it.

Most images finish inside this call, with the answer in `job.result`. A slower one answers with `job.status` queued or running: collect it with get_job and `job.id`. Calling this tool again would run the work again.

input_key.description: The image: the `input_key` upload_photo answered with, or a File ID the user copied from their CraterView.ai workspace.

tools.name: check_real
tools.description:
Real Check (cv-real-check-v2, free): Estimates whether an image was produced by a generative model (`generated`) rather than captured by a camera (`real`). `job.result.verdict` (`generated`, `real`, `uncertain`): Which way the evidence points. `job.result.generated_probability`: The estimated probability that the image was generated, from 0 to 1.

This check changes nothing and costs nothing, so it needs no go-ahead: call it when its answer would help, and say what it found.

Send the image as `input_key`: upload_photo answers with one.

An answer's `job` is the job as the API states it. On a finished job, `usage` is the account as get_usage answers it.

Most images finish inside this call, with the answer in `job.result`. A slower one answers with `job.status` queued or running: collect it with get_job and `job.id`. Calling this tool again would run the work again.

input_key.description: The image: the `input_key` upload_photo answered with, or a File ID the user copied from their CraterView.ai workspace.

tools.name: quote
tools.description:
Quote a CraterView.ai job without running it: what it would charge for this image, the settings it would send and, for an enlargement by scale, the result's size in megapixels. It never uploads, queues or charges anything.

Send the model and the params its tool would be sent, and the image as `input_key` — or, in place of it, image_width and image_height, which prices a file still on the user's computer without taking it off. For a link, call upload_photo first, which needs no asking.

An answer's `quote` is the quote as POST /v1/quotes states it, and `quote.params` is what to send the tool.

`credits_at_most`: In place of `credits`, where the price is not known yet: the most the job can be charged. A model priced by the faces it redraws knows only after the run, and a price by size needs the image's size.

input_key.description: The image: the `input_key` upload_photo answered with, or a File ID the user copied from their CraterView.ai workspace.

image_width.description: In place of the image: the image file's width in pixels.

image_height.description: In place of the image: the image file's height in pixels.

model.description: The model the job would run: cv-enhance-v3 is enhance_photo, cv-faces-v1 is redraw_small_faces, cv-headshot-v1 is make_headshot, cv-denoise-v1 is denoise_photo, cv-restore-v1 is restore_photo, cv-content-check-v1 is check_content, cv-real-check-v2 is check_real.

params.description: The params that tool would be sent.

tools.name: view_photo
tools.description:
Look at an image: an upload or a finished job's result, the whole of it or a part, as an image you can see.

Accepts `input_key` or `job_id`. Each look is a free job, needs no go-ahead and is not shown on the user's dashboard.

Look at the whole image first and then look closer. Each result includes the region of interest (`roi`) of the current view in fractions of the whole image, ready to send to a job. To look closer, set `within` to your current view and select `roi` as fractions within the current view. Repeat to zoom further.

input_key.description: The image: the `input_key` upload_photo answered with, or a File ID the user copied from their CraterView.ai workspace.

job_id.description: A finished job's `id`, to look at its result.

max_side.description: If needed, the returned view will be scaled down to have width and height within `max_side`.

roi.description: The region of the image to look at, as fractions of the width and height (from top left) of either the entire image or of another region in `within`.

within.description: The reference `roi`, typically one an earlier answer returned for this image.

tools.name: get_job
tools.description:
Read a CraterView.ai job: the result of one that had not finished, or fresh links to one that has.

Call this when a tool that runs a job returned a status of queued or running. It waits up to 25 seconds for the job to finish before answering, so there is no need to pause between calls: if it answers that the job is still queued or running, call it again.

`flagged`: Whether an automated check thought this job's images may fall outside what the service allows. A flag is a warning and does not stop the job. `null` means the images were not all checked.

job_id.description: The job's `id`, from the tool that ran it or from list_jobs.

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description:
The account's subscription status, credit balance, and which queue your next job goes to.

`community`: Whether your next job runs free on the community queue: smaller size limits on some models and longer waits at busy times. True without credit or a subscription, or once a limited subscription's monthly allowance is spent. Otherwise the job runs on paid compute.

`subscribed`: Whether the account has a live subscription, limited or unlimited. Stays true even after a limited subscription's credit allowance is spent. Read `community` to know if the next job would go to the free community queue or to the faster paid queue.

`credits_remaining` and `subscription_allowance_remaining`: Credits and subscription allowance remaining for the faster paid queue. Neither goes below zero. Zero does not block work, and no top-up is needed to run jobs. Read `community` to know if the next job would go to the free community queue or to the faster paid queue.

`subscription_allowance`: Allowance a limited subscription adds every month for paid compute. Null for an unlimited subscription or none. It adds nothing to `credits_remaining`.

The user buys credit or a subscription at https://craterview.ai/dashboard#buy; no tool buys anything.

tools.name: list_jobs
tools.description:
Your jobs, most recent first.

`flagged`: Whether an automated check thought this job's images may fall outside what the service allows. A flag is a warning and does not stop the job. `null` means the images were not all checked.

Use get_job with its `id` for more detail, such as the job's image links.

limit.description: How many jobs to list; 5 if left out.

before.description: Lists jobs older than this one: the answer's `next_before`, for the next page.

tools.name: keep_job_media
tools.description:
Retain this job's images past the ordinary expiry, because the owner asked.

To stop keeping them, the user does that in their job history at https://craterview.ai/dashboard; delete_job_media removes them now.

job_id.description: The job's `id`, from the tool that ran it or from list_jobs.

tools.name: delete_job_media
tools.description:
Delete this job's images now — the copy of your image the job worked from, the result, its preview, and any kept copy — rather than waiting for them to expire on schedule. A job you shared leaves the gallery with them. The file you uploaded is not part of the job: it is deleted on its own, shortly after the upload.

Not reversible: call this only after the user has said to.

job_id.description: The job's `id`, from the tool that ran it or from list_jobs.
